create_connection.description: Save a named connector configuration (credential included) so a connector query can reference it by name instead of carrying the token in every request. The connection is stored replicate-to-all — every node holds it, which is what lets each node fetch its own stripe of a distributed query straight from the source. Saving an existing name replaces it, re-sealing the new credential. The token is stored sealed (AES-256-GCM under a key derived from the cluster join token, never in the replicated catalogue) and is never returned by any surface (list_connections and system.connections report only whether one is set). Requires orchestration:create_connection.

create_dataset_from_query.description: Run a read-only query against an external source (Snowflake or Postgres) and load its rows into a new partitioned table placed across the cluster — the in-product path from a warehouse to a featurizable dataset, with no manual export. Only a single SELECT/WITH may run. A remote source is reached over the network with your credentials, so it is consent-gated when the node enforces governance; a loopback Postgres touches no cloud and runs directly (audited as dataset_added; visible in system.datasets). Requires orchestration:create_dataset_from_query. Consent-gated: on a node started with --governance this never executes on a plain call — it returns a one-time consent challenge that a DIFFERENT principal must approve (#621). Consent enforcement is off by default.

Anything a report would want and this run cannot supply is listed in `missing` with the reason, rather than left blank.
